newsitem.title: USA: CERBCO says court denies most of petition.
newsitem.headline: CERBCO says court denies most of petition.

text.p: CERBCO Inc said that in a case related to litigation brought against two company directors, a court denied most of a petition by plaintiffs' lawyers seeking about $1.6 million in fees and costs.
In April, the Delaware Supreme Court ordered two directors to pay damages for having used their board position to "usurp" for themselves a business deal intended for the company.

The plaintiff, Merle Thorpe, filed the suit in 1990 after learning that directors Robert Erikson and his brother George told Instituform of North America to negotiate with them, rather than with CERBCO, to buy a controlling interest in CERBCO's major asset, Insituform East Inc.
In a decision on remand, the Delaware Court of Chancery determined the plaintiffs' attorneys should receive only $143,364 in fees and $9,222 in costs against the Eriksons.
Company officials were not immediately available to comment further.
